That's marginally. TLT ability is worth H (3-5) points each time it's played. It was said that it was simply better. Simply better means if it does 1 damage it, it now does 2. I am not saying it is overall better, but it is not "simply" better. It doesn't do the same thing as the original just more.

I do think you are underestimating Tachy's original ability. The only way TLT can put cards into her trash is by playing them. That means, every turn you aren't playing a Burst, you are losing some damage from Sonic Vortex and Lightspeed Barrage. This means that playing Hypersonic Assault actually decreases TLT damage (although it might be worth it), or you wont be able to wait for the best time to play a particular Burst, becuase you need it in the trash.

Research Grant also negates the issue. If you plan on using Research Grant anyways, then it doesn't matter what her base power is. Of course, you can use her base power until you get Research Grant, but that just means there are different strategies.

Tachy herself already has many ways to draw cards, and even a few ways to have everyone else draw cards. Having everyone draw 2 cards a turn instead of 1 is a big deal, but having everyone draw 3 instead of 2 doesn't have the same effect.

Before you start comparing the "points" you have to conisder:

1) How many turns TLT will use her base power. If there are only 6 rounds in a game, and you start using Research Grant after round 3, you only get points for the first 3 rounds, not every round.

2) How often Tachy and the other heroes will already be drawing cards. The more cards drawn, the less effective the ability is. In addition, if a hero has already reached there "perfect" setup, additional cards won't really matter.

3) If a villain needs a big burst of damage. With some villains having a big burst of damage could be extremely important.

4) How many villain targets come out. Great I have an extra card, I just wish I had another burst in the trash so that I can hit all the targets I need to this turn, instead of playing a burst.

I am not saying that TLT isn't better, but she isn't "simply" better.

EDIT: Just to clarify, Sensei Fixer's ability is "simply" better. There is absolutely no reason not to take his ability over normal Fixer's. While TLT might be better in many situations, I wouldn't automatically pick it over original Tachy. It would depend on who the villain is, and who the other heroes are.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
You also don't apply a target's soak to other targets - if you're hitting Condemnation for two with Dual Crowbars, it'll only take one as it has one point of soak. If your second target is then Apostate (assuming no Fiendish Pugilists are out), he'll still take two. It's only Condemnation's personal soak that blocks one damage - this doesn't extend to other targets. Similarly, if you tried hitting Condemnation with the Crowbars for two damage and the Orb was out, the damage would be redirected to the Orb and remain at two points because the Orb has no soak. Then you could still choose the Orb as your second target and whack it again for two, because your first target was Condemnation - it just got redirected.

If you'd instead used the Jack Handle, you'd attempt to deal your base damage to everything, but only the things with soak would block it - you wouldn't apply the same soak to everything if those targets didn't have any.

The reason I think this now is because Fixer's deck has different cards specialized for a task (and few draw abilities): what brings this together is a main power that helps you dig for those. Each turn you face a decision if you should discard to dig, and then what to discard. Even if you start with the cards you want, it takes at least 3 turns to put them down (style/tool/harmony) you'll always want more Overdrives, Charge, Salvage Yard or Grease Gun.

So basically IMO phanta was spot on on this, quite some time ago.

I think it's relevant to say that I have been playing style/tools reversed: styles go back to hand and tools get destroyed. It's another thing that just feels more intuitive and thematic when playing. He drops a weapon to grab another but he doesn't forget how to fight and can go back to how he was doing it five minutes ago. It also feels more cohesive with Salvage yard. Dunno how much it changes (I rarely changed stances/tools) but I liked it.

Oh, also changed Riveting Crane in that it still works if it's reduced to exactly 0 damage (not below). Basically if you can deal as much damage as the target has reduction, you break their reduction. In another sense, it's like a ghostly +1 for targets that have damage reduction. Felt RT needed a bit of love to work as-is, specially early game when DR is common in a lot of Villains.

My favorite version of Fixer is:

Mr. Fixer deals 1 target 0 melee damage. You may draw a card or discard a card, if you discarded another player may draw a card.

His damage is lowered to compensate for the extra utility.  As you said in your post above it really helps him dig for those cards he wants and needs. It also plays into a more team support roll as after you have plenty of cards in your hand you can start getting rid of them to help others draw extra.  Of course it is completely a personal choice but this is may favorite version of Fixer that I have used by far.  I doubt I'll ever play the normal fixer ever again, but the Dark Watch one is still quite interesting.
